title: Targeted circuit breaker for prefetch saturation across Hosted/Dedicated
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported recurrent p99/p999 tail latency spikes and partial request stalls during mixed-length traffic waves. Root cause analysis points to prefetch/admission saturation in the continuous batcher: when a burst of long-context requests arrives, prefetch admission consumes the inflight admission reservoir and forces aggressive KV eviction and large-batch formation. This starves latency-sensitive short requests and amplifies a long-context tail. Impact spans Hosted and Dedicated regions; a small number of Private deployments surfaced similar behavior during private upgrade windows.

Why this ticket: Customers (notably Aegis Health and LexiconAI) opened escalations with production traces showing stalled small-request throughput and multi-second tail regressions. We need a quick, low-risk mitigation (circuit-breaker + targeted backpressure) that can be rolled to Hosted first, then Dedicated, with a long-term follow-up refactor of admission heuristics.

Scope: Implement a tenant-aware, prefetch admission circuit-breaker that: (1) bounds the prefetch/admission fraction of the inflight reservoir per tenant; (2) applies an aging priority boost to short/latency-sensitive requests; (3) emits detailed telemetry for admitted/rejected prefetch attempts. The change must be configurable (per-tenant and per-deployment) and default to safe conservative thresholds in Hosted.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of scheduler admission policy or changing KV cache eviction policy in this hotfix. Those are follow-ups after telemetry confirms effectiveness.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay production trace captured from Aegis Health (s3://prod-traces/2026-02-26-aegis-wave-1.json) on staging runtime-1.24.0 with mixed-length generator load (30% long-context >8k tokens, 70% short <128 tokens).
2) Launch coordinated microburst (500 concurrent long-context sessions sustained for 60s) with background short-request steady traffic (200 rps).

3) Observe admission reservoir depletion metrics: admission_inflight_window_saturation >= 0.95, continuous_batcher_prefetch_success_rate drops, p99 short-request latency spikes to >800ms, backend queue backlog rising.
4) Collect kv_cache_evictions, batch_size distribution, and per-tenant admission rejections for postmortem.
recent_activity: 2026-03-01: Triage call with PM and SRE; elevated priority after customer escalation. Assigned to Marco Ruiz.
2026-03-03: Reproduced on staging using Aegis trace; confirmed prefetch admission dominates reservation and causes eviction churn.
2026-03-05: Instrumentation PR landed for detailed admission metrics (GH-11234).
2026-03-08: Prototype circuit-breaker implemented in branch feat/ingress-circuit-breaker (runtime repo).
2026-03-10: Canary run on two Hosted nodes showed 40% reduction in short-request p99 during synthetic wave.
2026-03-13: Design review with product & SRE; agreed on conservative defaults and per-tenant opt-in for Dedicated during initial rollout.
2026-03-14: Preparing rollout playbook and communication for impacted customers; ticket moved to In Progress.
decision_log: Decision 1 (2026-03-05): Add admission telemetry before mitigation to quantify per-tenant pressure. Rationale: avoid masking root cause and gather data for long-term fixes.

Decision 2 (2026-03-11): Implement circuit-breaker that caps prefetch admission to 40% of reservoir by default, with priority aging for short requests. Rationale: reduces starvation while preserving long-request throughput.

Decision 3 (2026-03-13): Rollout plan: Hosted default ON (conservative thresholds); Dedicated OFF by default and enabled per-customer after verification; Private customers to receive advisory and opt-in patch. Rationale: minimize blast radius for Dedicated/Private tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Deploy to staging with full telemetry and synthetic workload (3/15). Phase 1: Canary on 2 Hosted nodes for 48h, monitor p50/p95/p99 for short and long flows, KV eviction rate, admission_reject_rate (3/16-3/17). Phase 2: Gradual Hosted rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 3 days if metrics stable. Phase 3: Offer Dedicated customers opt-in toggle; for opt-in requests perform dry-run and metrics review before enabling. Rollback: revert config or disable circuit-breaker if short-request p99 increases by >10% or error rate >0.5%.
qa_checks: End-to-end regression test harness reproduces mixed-length waves and asserts short-request p99 reduction.
Unit tests for circuit-breaker thresholds and per-tenant accounting.
Load test: soak 1k RPS mixed workload for 1 hour on staging and validate KV eviction delta < 20% vs baseline.
Observability: new dashboard panels visible in console and alerts for admission_reject_rate spikes.
Canary health check: 0 critical errors and latency SLOs met for two consecutive 15-minute windows before rollout step up.
postmortem_followups: 1) Long-term: Refactor admission policy with workload-aware reservoir allocation (owner: Lina Gomez, estimate: 13 pts).
2) Add tenant-priority SLA metadata so platform can bias admission for latency-sensitive tiers (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 8 pts).
3) Improve synthetic workload library with richer long-context replay scenarios and integrate into CI (owner: QA team, estimate: 5 pts).
4) Document mitigation and add an automated alert/auto-toggle runbook for future incidents (owner: SRE, estimate: 3 pts).
